content: MK says the Naqshbandi connection proved most problematic for the next generation: despite Ṣāʾin al-Dīn's warm relations with Khwāja Ḥasan ʿAṭṭār, his recognition as preeminent lettrist by the Naqshbandi Kāshifīs (father and son), and Yazdī's appearance in the Rashaḥāt-i ʿAyn al-Ḥayāt as a promoter of Ibn ʿArabī, Jāmī appears to have been at pains to minimize the Isfahan Circle's importance and quarantine them intellectually.
